title: Cycle-Finding Complexity Under Component Conditioning
summary: An offline estimate heuristically treats cycle-finding costs as stable under component conditioning; proving this or quantifying the resulting gap remains open.

formal_statement.body: An offline precomputation complexity estimate for detecting a large component with a small cycle uses a heuristic assumption about cycle-finding costs. [S1] The assumption is that the average complexity of finding a cycle from a random point of a random function is not significantly different from the average complexity of finding a cycle from a fixed random function conditioned on having a $\nu$-component. [S1] The unresolved task is to prove this similarity or quantify the difference between the two average complexities under that conditioning. [S1]

scope.domain: Random-function cycle statistics for offline precomputation in symmetric cryptanalysis.
assumptions: The average complexity of cycle finding from a random point of a random function does not significantly differ from that for a random point of a fixed random function conditioned to have a ν-component.
parameters: ν: parameter appearing in the ν-component condition on the fixed random function
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove the claimed similarity or quantify the difference between the two average cycle-finding complexities under ν-component conditioning.

citations.label: Generic Attack on Duplex-Based AEAD Modes using Random Function Statistics

progress.summary: The paper presents the offline precomputation estimate as heuristic because it relies on a conditional cycle-finding complexity comparison. It argues that significant distortion is unlikely but does not establish the comparison rigorously.
citation_labels: Henri Gilbert et al., Generic Attack on Duplex-Based AEAD Modes using Random Function Statistics
